clue.text: This will explain how to cook prime piece of rump, juicy piece

definitions.text: This will explain how to cook

indicators.note: prime means first or foremost, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept
something juicy is squashed and squelchy, so the word after it is mashed into a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of rump
the letters of piece rearranged

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction about preparing a cut of rump steak and a succulent morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole opening phrase: a RECIPE is the thing that explains how to cook. 'Piece' appears twice; only the second is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is the set of written instructions telling a cook how to prepare a dish.

clue.text: Form of street dance associated with jerks?

definitions.text: Form of street dance associated with jerks?

blocks.note: surface reading: a breakdance style, the robot, with stiff mechanical moves
setter's reading: the field of building machines, whose movements are jerky

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the dance-sounding name doubles as the science of mechanical automata.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotics is the engineering of automated machines, and doing the robot dance mimics their jerky motion.

clue.text: Bananas and nuts, they may be on the table at Christmas

definitions.text: they may be on the table at Christmas

blocks.note: first meaning: crazy, both words being slang for mad

blocks.clueFragment: they may be on the table at Christmas
blocks.note: second meaning: paper tubes that bang when pulled apart at dinner

explanation.walkthrough: Bananas and nuts look like festive food; both are slang for mad. Christmas crackers are British paper tubes pulled with a bang, holding a hat and a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is British slang for insane, and crackers are also the festive novelties laid at each place setting.

clue.text: Extremely perceptive foreign spy becomes a diarist

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the two end letters of the following word
foreign means strange and altered, so the word after it is rearranged

blocks.note: the first and last letters of perceptive
the letters of spy rearranged

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed overseas agent turns to writing a journal.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys kept a famous diary of 1660s London, so he is the archetypal diarist.

clue.text: I appear in these French skating exhibitions

blocks.note: taken as written
the French demonstrative ce (ces in the plural)
to show up is to appear

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of featuring in some French skating displays.
explanation.walkthrough: French 'these' is strictly CES; the setter takes just CE, the demonstrative's base form, and lets SHOWS supply the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice shows are theatrical spectacles performed by skaters on a rink, so they are skating exhibitions.

clue.text: Caught with joint in prison

blocks.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a link is a joint or connection

explanation.surface: Someone is arrested with a cannabis cigarette while in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint suggests a cannabis cigarette; it means a connecting piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Clink is informal slang for a jail, from an old London prison of that name.

clue.text: Father Christmas, very large, captured by artist in a California city

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so the artist's letters enclose what precedes

blocks.note: Santa Claus is Father Christmas
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
OS means outsize, very large

explanation.surface: A painter catches a huge Santa on canvas somewhere in California.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts, and OS, the clothing size outsize, are crossword staples.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Rosa is a city in Sonoma County in northern California.

clue.text: Broken coal in a fuel container

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the following letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: the letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: Smashed lumps of coal lie inside a fuel bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' belongs to the fodder rather than linking.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilcan is a metal can for holding oil, a liquid fuel or lubricant.

clue.text: Hanging on's no time for talking!

indicators.note: no means without, so the word loses the letter that follows

blocks.note: staying is hanging on, remaining
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that someone who lingers has no time to chat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Hanging on' reads as 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying is the act of uttering words, so it serves as a gerund meaning speaking or talking.

clue.text: Scholar holding old scarf

indicators.note: holding means grasping something inside, so the scholar's letters wrap round the next piece

blocks.note: a Bachelor of Arts is a graduate scholar
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An academic clutching a worn-out old scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a long fluffy scarf, typically of feathers, worn round the neck.

clue.text: With fervour, oppose religious drama

blocks.note: passion is intense fervour
to play a team is to oppose it in a match

explanation.surface: Someone vehemently objects to a play about religion.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'With fervour' modify 'oppose', but the two words are separate pieces placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A passion play is a dramatic staging of Christ's suffering and death, performed by religious communities.

clue.text: English artist's wintry figure?

blocks.note: surface reading: a painted figure in a snowy landscape by an English painter
setter's reading: a figure built of snow, and the famous picture book by English illustrator Raymond Briggs

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark points to Raymond Briggs, the English illustrator whose wordless book became a Christmas film.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure made of snow is the classic wintry figure, and Briggs's book of that title is a British Christmas favourite.

clue.text: Assess and buy shares

blocks.note: first meaning: to review a situation and weigh it up
second meaning: literally to acquire stock in a company

explanation.surface: An investor sizes up a company and then invests in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pausing to evaluate a situation, while read literally it means acquiring company stock.

clue.text: Another military commander elected

definitions.note: used as in 'another go': once more

blocks.note: an aga is a commander in the Ottoman Empire
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: One more army general has won an election.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA, a Turkish title for an officer or chief, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for 'another' means wanting the thing once more, which is what again expresses.

clue.text: Noel has to fight for a bonus

blocks.note: Noel is another name for the festive season
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A man named Noel must go into the ring to earn some extra money.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel looks like a man's name. A Christmas box is a British tip given at Christmas to postmen, refuse collectors and other tradespeople.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas box is a seasonal gratuity given to service workers, an extra payment or bonus.

clue.text: One miser's uncertain what vicars do?

indicators.note: uncertain means unsettled or unfixed, so the letters before it have no fixed order

blocks.note: the letters of these words, with the S, rearranged

explanation.surface: A stingy person is unsure what clergymen actually get up to.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicars preach sermons, and to sermonise is to deliver one or moralise at length, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Makes a mistake and falls over

blocks.note: first meaning: blunders
second meaning: literally slips and goes up in the air

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy gets something wrong and takes a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means errs, while its literal sense is losing footing and tumbling.

clue.text: Old boy's story about cold bar

indicators.note: about means around, so the story wraps round the following piece

blocks.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil, plus the S
a tale is a story
C is the standard abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: An old school friend tells an anecdote about a chilly pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar looks like a pub to suit the story; it is a verb-turned-noun meaning a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar is a barrier that blocks progress, just as an obstacle does.

clue.text: Exclamation from pop star dropping ring

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of something, so a letter falls out of the name

blocks.note: Boy George is the Culture Club singer
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A singer shouts out after losing a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: By George is an old-fashioned interjection of surprise or emphasis, so it is an exclamation.

clue.text: Head lad gets a part in panto

blocks.note: the head of a school or college is its principal
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: The head boy at school is cast in the Christmas pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: Panto, the British Christmas pantomime, traditionally casts a young woman as the hero, the PRINCIPAL BOY.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal boy is the leading young male role in a pantomime, so it is a part in one.

clue.text: Christmas decoration causing violent anger around Egypt's capital

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the anger encloses what follows
capital means the head letter of a word, so only the first letter of Egypt is used

blocks.note: wrath is fierce anger
the first letter of Egypt

explanation.surface: A festive ornament provokes fury in Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: Egypt's capital reads as Cairo; it means the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath of holly or evergreens is hung on doors as a festive ornament.

clue.text: Article takes shape identifying spirits

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
a plan that gels takes shape

explanation.surface: A newspaper story begins to identify ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: Angels are heavenly spiritual beings, so they count as spirits.

clue.text: Call round for drummer

blocks.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone phones around looking for a percussionist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer, so the name stands for a famous percussionist.

clue.text: Semi to let out - it may get you a few smackers

definitions.text: it may get you a few smackers

indicators.note: out suggests disorder or being put wrong, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these three words rearranged

explanation.surface: A semi-detached house is up for rent and might bring in a little money.
explanation.walkthrough: Smackers looks like slang for pounds or dollars, as a rental would bring; here they are smacking kisses.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition says anyone standing under hanging mistletoe may be kissed, so it can earn you a few kisses.

clue.text: I am to be found in Michigan tourist centre

indicators.note: to be found in means located within, so the phrase sits inside the state abbreviation

blocks.note: MI is the US postal abbreviation for Michigan
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says they are in Michigan visiting a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Michigan seems to be a location, which jars with the answer being in Florida; it is only an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami in Florida is a major holiday destination famous for beaches and nightlife.

clue.text: Subject, for example, in fiction

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the example abbreviation sits inside the fiction

blocks.note: a lie is a fiction, an untruth
eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An illustrative topic from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Subject suggests a topic; it is a person owing allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege in feudal usage can be a vassal bound to serve a lord, so a subject.

clue.text: I am a creep in comic film

indicators.note: comic suggests clowning about, so the preceding letters are jumbled for fun

blocks.note: the letters of these four words rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor confesses to playing a sleazy character in a comedy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic film' reads as one phrase, but comic is the signal and film alone is the definition. 'In' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: American Pie is a 1999 teen comedy film, so the title names a film.

clue.text: Some Jamaica rum in vehicle

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the letters sit inside the neighbouring words

blocks.note: spans the end of Jamaica and start of rum

explanation.surface: Someone stashes a bottle of Caribbean rum in their car.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a motor vehicle for carrying people on roads.

clue.text: Skipper perished at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the word before is scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of perished rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's captain died during a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Skipper looks like a ship's captain, which fits 'at sea' perfectly; it is a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesperids are the family of small, darting butterflies commonly called skippers.

clue.text: Tranquil piece of music a daughter brought out

indicators.note: brought out means taken away from inside, so these letters are removed from the middle

blocks.note: a serenade is a musical composition
taken as written
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A calm composition that a girl performed or published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought out' suggests a daughter releasing a song; it means A and D are lifted out of the music.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene describes something calm and untroubled, a direct synonym of tranquil.
